# Description: this is a reusable workflow that runs e2e tests.
#
# See `./test-prs.yml` to see an example usage.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      commit:
        # commit to run tests against
        required: true
        type: string
      repository:
        # repository to run tests against (possibly a fork of amplify-ui)
        required: true
        type: string
      skip-changed-packages-check:
        # skip checking changed packages job if true
        required: false
        default: 'false'
        type: string

    secrets:
      AUTH_E2E_ROLE_ARN:
        required: true
      GEO_E2E_ROLE_ARN:
        required: true
      STORAGE_E2E_ROLE_ARN:
        required: true
      DATASTORE_E2E_ROLE_ARN:
        required: true
      IN_APP_MESSAGING_E2E_ROLE_ARN:
        required: true
      LIVENESS_E2E_ROLE_ARN:
        required: true
      AI_E2E_ROLE_ARN:
        required: true
      DOMAIN:
        required: true
      PHONE_NUMBER:
        required: true
      USERNAME:
        required: true
      NEW_PASSWORD:
        required: true
      VALID_PASSWORD:
        required: true
      SITE_URL:
        required: true
      DOCSEARCH_DOCS_APP_ID:
        required: true
      DOCSEARCH_DOCS_API_KEY:
        required: true
      DOCSEARCH_DOCS_INDEX_NAME:
        required: true

jobs:
  e2e:
    # Only run e2e tests if unit tests pass
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: ci
    env:
      NODE_ENV: test

    strategy:
      # Run each examples (e.g. `next-example`) which uses a library (e.g. `@aws-amplify/ui-react`)
      # BUT, Exclude `@todo-${{ package }}` tests in PRs
      # See: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflow-syntax-for-github-actions#using-environment-variables-in-a-matrix
      matrix:
        include:
          - example: angular
            package: angular
            resource-path: ui/components/authenticator/sign-in-with-username
            tags: '@angular and not @todo-angular'

          - example: next
            package: react
            resource-path: ui/components/authenticator/sign-in-with-username
            tags: '@react and not @todo-react'

          - example: react-router
            package: react
            tags: '@react-router and not @todo-react-router'

          - example: next-app-router
            package: react
            tags: '@next-app-router and not @todo-next-app-router'

          - example: vue
            package: vue
            resource-path: ui/components/authenticator/sign-in-with-username
            tags: '@vue and not @todo-vue'

          - example: svelte
            package: svelte
            resource-path: ui/components/authenticator/sign-in-with-username
            tags: '@svelte and not @todo-svelte'

    steps:
      - name: Checkout Amplify UI
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7.0.0
        with:
          # For `pull_request_target`, we want ref to point to `pull_request.head.ref` because `github.ref`
          # always points to the target branch.
          # See: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/learn-github-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows
          ref: ${{ inputs.commit }}
          repository: ${{ inputs.repository }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Next.js Cache
        uses: actions/cache@27d5ce7f107fe9357f9df03efb73ab90386fccae # v5.0.5
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/.next/cache
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-nextjs-${{ hash

name: Checks

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # submodules: the SoloPlay submodule cannot be checked in isolation (its tsconfig points at
      # ../../sdk and ../../libs), so the parent checkout is where it gets validated - against the
      # exact commit this repo pins.
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      # Node 24: eslint-plugin-es-x@10 requires ^22.23.0 || ^24.18.0 || >=26.4.0, and
      # eslint@10 requires ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24. Anything older cannot run the toolchain.
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # lint:check, never `lint` - that one is `eslint --fix`, which would rewrite files in CI
      # and let anything auto-fixable pass silently.
      - name: ESLint
        run: npm run lint:check

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      # The no-undef inventory is generated. If someone adds a global without regenerating,
      # the committed file goes stale and no-undef quietly stops covering it.
      - name: Globals inventory is current
        run: npm run globals:check

      - name: Typecheck (SoloPlay submodule)
        run: npm run typecheck:soloplay

      # Every runtime .js must belong to a TS program. A file in none gets no typechecking and
      # no editor intellisense, and nothing else reports it.
      - name: No orphaned files
        run: node tools/audit/program-files.mjs --check
